speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs how is the Home Team prepared for multiple concurrent civil unrest incidents without significantly compromising its routine incident response responsibilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Public assemblies in Singapore are regulated under the Public Order Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: A Police permit is required to hold a public assembly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Clear guidelines are given to event organisers during their permit application.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For example, they are required to conduct their events in a socially responsible manner and ensure that they do not cause any danger or undue alarm to the general public.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They are also advised to give due consideration to ensure that public safety, security, law and order are not compromised during the event.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For example, in an area where POSSPA powers have been authorised, the Police may impose a cordon around the target area and order any vehicle or individual within the cordon to leave or be removed, close public roads within or leading to or from the target area, or impose a curfew requiring every person in the target area to remain indoors within specified hours.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Such powers allow the Police to take decisive measures if the need arises to prevent public order incidents from escalating.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Government has in place a crisis management system to prepare for and respond to major incidents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: If necessary, the Singapore Police Force can also draw on specialist forces.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Special Operations Command (SOC) troopers are trained to handle such situations.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: There are various ways to assist the Home Team in this area.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The first is for the public to take in SGSecure messages and, if possible, to train.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: During major incidents, the public can also play a very important role by adhering to official advisories from authorities, such as the Police's advisories to keep out of harm's way.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Members of the public can also help the Home Team by staying vigilant and reporting any useful information to the authorities.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: It is also important for the public to always refer to official sources of information.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: They should be discerning regarding the information they receive and to be mindful not to share information, photos, videos that can lead to panic or fear.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Distortions, rumours, untruths, misinformation and spams can spread very quickly, especially through social media, and can cause confusion.
